key_insight: Tuning Ti-substituted SrVO₃ toward a metal-insulator transition broadens its optical window, with an optimal composition range balancing transparency and conductivity near the transition.
engineering_relevance: This materials-design strategy could improve transparent electrodes for silicon photovoltaics, though the abstract does not report solar-cell device performance or AI methods.
method: Use epitaxial Ti-substituted SrVO₃ films to tune electronic filling and proximity to the metal-insulator transition.
Track optical transparency, metallic transport, and near-Fermi-level spectral weight.
Evaluate the transparency–conductivity balance using the Haacke figure of merit.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports systematic optical-window broadening into regimes relevant to silicon photovoltaics and a figure-of-merit optimum near the transition, without numerical performance values.
watch_item: Carrier depletion and disorder reduce coherent transport near the transition, limiting how far transparency can be improved without sacrificing conductivity.
paper_title: Engineering Correlated Transparent Conductors via Metal-Insulator Transition Proximity
